evidence: The retention mechanism is real, but the required end-to-end demonstration breaks at the final stated-requirement contradiction. Concrete source-level trace: (1) Keep one connected Watch run, one pending Lazy invitation and fixed render shape. Each actual topic change can become a new canonical context: src/store/invitation_content.rs:16-38 publishes the latest thread revision; :1148-1175 replaces the same binding/invitation/consumer item and resets its partial/complete counters when context.key changes. Allow each change to be pulled before making the next change, so canonical coalescing does not skip it. (2) src/cli/watch.rs:690-711 writes/flushes each bounded Watch page and confirms its token independently of JS append. (3) First invitation line enters register.js:296-314 and starts append at :543-554. Hold that promise unresolved, or repeatedly resolve it with deny while preserving the same run. (4) Each distinct topic_revision/command_context_epoch misses both delivered-version suppression (:282-284) and pending-version deduplication (:289-294), adding another body. appendInflight blocks another append (:544); ordinary deny retains same-run items and merely backs off (:568-572, discardStale :154-161). After n distinct successfully streamed contexts the queue retains n bodies. The 1024 cap (:336-338) is only the delivered invitationVersions map. (5) If append later succeeds, complete removes only its captured invitation object (:327), then pumpLazy selects every remaining passive revision into one frame (:546-554). Thus pending-body storage and recovery framing grow with revision history; existing manual-append tests at integrations/claude/mod/tests/delivery.test.ts:1973-1998 and :2038-2059 cover the first two retained contexts, not a bound. Base 565def86 register.js:250 rejected invitation items and :273 deduplicated other items solely by id, so this particular same-invitation history is newly enabled, not a pre-existing finding. However, the selected contract does not promise a bounded JS pending queue, bounded session.append frame, append timeout, or coalescing of already-flushed downstream revisions. TRUST-POLICY.md:1544-1557 explicitly bounds canonical consumer/item bookkeeping and states eventual latest context after quiescence, without promising every transient revision. :1658-1683 bounds the canonical current outbox and actual native-codec/Watch output, not the JS aggregate append. task-15-bounded-design-dispositions.md:54 and :88-90 explicitly choose complete emit+flush as FULL OFFER evidence for Watch, introduce no modappend proof/confirmation obligation, and limit offers per unchanged key; different genuine revisions do not violate that bound. resume-v090-q3-channel-design.md:87-89 separately disclaims a transport-memory cap/queue redesign; this is not proof that the JS queue is bounded, but it also supplies no missing JS cap. During a perpetual unresolved/denied append no downstream success is demonstrated; after any finite revision sequence and successful append recovery the latest queued context is included and eventually completed, satisfying the stated eventual-latest guarantee. Canonical state still coalesces and every original Watch page remains within its own limit. A coalesced latest pending JS revision would improve this behavior, but requiring it here would add a downstream resource guarantee to the spec. No runtime experiment is needed to resolve this internal structural claim; the missing final requirement, rather than the queue mechanism, prevents CONFIRM under the REPRODUCE rubric.
